events.title: Osborne 1 released
events.summary: Osborne Computer Corporation began shipping the Osborne 1 in April 1981 — the first commercially successful portable computer.
events.about: The Osborne 1 weighed 24 pounds with a 5-inch screen and dual floppy drives — users carried a complete CP/M system between home and office. Its bundled software bundle pioneered the "killer app" sales model. Though short-lived as a company, Osborne proved demand for luggable computers before the IBM PC dominated portables.

narrative.whyChosen: The Osborne 1 was the first mass-market portable microcomputer sold to businesses.
narrative.whyImportant: It established the portable form factor and software-bundle strategy for early PC vendors.
narrative.problemSolved: Professionals needed to run business software away from the office without access to a desktop machine.
